deepdive.photo_tips: 飛行塔を前景に大阪平野を入れる構図が定番。夕方は西〜北西側から逆光気味に夜景へ切り替えると映える。公式ページに撮影禁止の明記は見当たらないが、遊具運転中の立入制限は厳守。[公式HP 絶景ポイント](https://www.ikomasanjou.com/scenery/)
deepdive.trivia:
- 飛行塔は現存する国内最古の大型遊具とされ、山上のシンボルになっている。[Wikipedia日本語版](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E7%94%9F%E9%A7%92%E5%B1%B1%E4%B8%8A%E9%81%8A%E5%9C%92%E5%9C%B0)
- 県境にまたがる遊園地として知られるが、遊具自体は登記上は生駒市側にあると報じられている。[産経ニュース](https://www.sankei.com/article/20251204-DCZEMKIPNRO3RGOMQEHMGZQWOM/)
- 生駒ケーブルは鳥居前駅〜宝山寺駅間で別デザインの車両が交代するため、移動自体が観光体験になる。[近鉄 生駒ケーブルカーのまめ知識](https://www.kintetsu.co.jp/senden/ikoma_cable/about/)
deepdive.warnings_extra: 山上は麓よりかなり涼しく、夕方以降は体感温度が下がるため防寒を。乗り物や展望施設では係員の指示を優先し、他の来園者の写り込みにも配慮すること。

deepdive.history_jp_en: Ikoma Sanjo Yuenchi (Ikoma Mountain Summit Amusement Park) was developed by the predecessor of Kintetsu — the Osaka Electric Railway (Osaka Denki Kido) — as part of its railway-corridor development, and opened on March 27, 1929 (Showa 4), in conjunction with the extension of the Ikoma Cable Sanjosen (mountain summit line). According to the Ikoma City Digital Museum, tree planting and water supply and drainage infrastructure were also developed at the time of opening, and rides such as the Hiko-to (Flying Tower) were installed. The opening catchphrase was "Summer's Cool Line," selling the resort as a leisure destination that offered the coolness and panoramic views of the summit. The Flying Tower, symbolic of the park, is regarded as the oldest surviving large-scale amusement ride in Japan; it is said to have been used as an anti-aircraft surveillance tower during the war. After the war the park continued to be updated as a leisure base of the Kintetsu Group, and following the introduction of free admission in 1999 and the "PLAY PEAK ITADAKI" concept in 2019, the park continues in its present form. [Ikoma City Digital Museum](https://www.city.ikoma.lg.jp/html/dm/bun/shosai/yuenchi/yuenchi.html), [Wikipedia (Japanese)](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E7%94%9F%E9%A7%92%E5%B1%B1%E4%B8%8A%E9%81%8A%E5%9C%92%E5%9C%B0)
deepdive.cultural_context_jp_en: This mountaintop resort was built by a modern private railway to stimulate suburban demand, and is a classic example of "railway-corridor development" that combined summer retreat, scenic views, and light entertainment. The core value lies in the coolness at 642 meters elevation and the panoramic view over the Osaka Plain; today the retro scenery and night-view experience are being re-evaluated. [Ikoma City Digital Museum](https://www.city.ikoma.lg.jp/html/dm/bun/shosai/yuenchi/yuenchi.html), [Official website — Scenic Viewpoints](https://www.ikomasanjou.com/scenery/)
deepdive.local_perspective_jp_en: It is introduced in Ikoma City's official materials as a historical asset of the city, and Kintetsu's own communications position it as the core of "Ikoma Retro" branding. Locally, it is cherished as Nara Prefecture's only amusement park and remains a popular destination for families and night-view visitors. [Ikoma City Digital Museum](https://www.city.ikoma.lg.jp/html/dm/bun/shosai/yuenchi/yuenchi.html), [Kintetsu "Ikoma Retro"](https://www.kintetsu.co.jp/senden/ikomaretro/)

In the evening, switching to the night view with slight backlighting from the west-to-northwest is effective. No explicit photography prohibition is noted on the official page, but access restrictions around operating rides must be strictly observed. deepdive.trivia_en:

- The Ikoma Cable Car uses different vehicle designs between Torii-mae Station and Hozan-ji Station, so the journey itself becomes part of the tourist experience. [Kintetsu — Ikoma Cable Car Trivia](https://www.kintetsu.co.jp/senden/ikoma_cable/about/)
deepdive.warnings_extra_en: The mountaintop is considerably cooler than the foothills, and body temperature drops sharply after evening — please bring appropriate warm clothing. On rides and at observation facilities, follow staff instructions and be mindful of other visitors appearing in your photographs.

name: 旧奈良監獄（ならまちごぜんと）
name_kana: きゅうならかんごく
address: 奈良県奈良市般若寺町18
fee: ホテル宿泊・見学ツアー参加で体験可
hours: 見学ツアー開催日による
summary: 明治41年（1908年）竣工の赤レンガ建築の少年刑務所。日本に5つ現存する「明治の五大監獄」の一つで、ヨーロッパの監獄建築を模した扇形・放射状の建物構造が独特。2017年に少年刑務所として閉所後、歴史的建物を活かしたホテル・ミュージアムとして2023年に再開業。「元少年刑務所のホテルに泊まれる」という唯一無二の体験が可能。監獄の独房・中庭・礼拝堂を日帰り見学できるツアーもある。奈良公園から徒歩圏という立地の「観光地×監獄」。
highlights: 「元少年刑務所のホテルに泊まれる」という非日常性
明治の赤レンガ建築が保存された貴重な建物
監獄の独房・放射状廊下の構造が生み出す独特の空間感
from_kameyama: 近鉄で約1時間30分

deepdive.history_jp: 旧奈良監獄は、明治政府が監獄の国際標準化を進めた流れのなかで、1901年（明治34年）に改築計画が始まり、1908年（明治41年）に竣工した近代刑務所建築である。設計は司法技師・山下啓次郎で、中央の看守所から舎房が放射状に伸びる「ハビランド・システム」を採用した。江戸期の奈良奉行所・奈良監獄署の系譜を引きつつ、1909年（明治42年）に現在地で開設され、1946年（昭和21年）に奈良少年刑務所へ改称、2017年（平成29年）に閉鎖された。明治五大監獄の一つで、唯一全貌が残る遺構として、2017年2月23日に重要文化財に指定された。[旧奈良監獄アーカイブス](https://hoshinoresorts.com/nara-prison-museum/research-info/ja/history/), [奈良市ホームページ](https://www.city.nara.lg.jp/site/bunkazai/6912.html), [明治の五大監獄](https://hoshinoresorts.com/nara-prison-museum/research-info/ja/history/meiji-five-prison/)
deepdive.cultural_context_jp: 近代国家が「懲らしめ」から「矯正」へと刑罰観を移し、衛生・監視・分類を重視した施設として生まれた。放射状配置は受刑者管理の合理化を、赤レンガと西洋式意匠は司法制度の近代化を象徴する。今日では負の遺産を保存しつつ、建築・刑罰史・地域観光を横断する学習資源として再解釈されている。[旧奈良監獄アーカイブス](https://hoshinoresorts.com/nara-prison-museum/research-info/ja/), [奈良監獄ミュージアム公式](https://hoshinoresorts.com/nara-prison-museum/ja/), [法務省PDF](https://www.moj.go.jp/content/001225663.pdf)
deepdive.local_perspective_jp: 奈良市では文化財としての価値を前提に、見学会や保存活用の説明を行ってきた。閉鎖後も「地域の近代化の記憶」を伝える施設として関心が高く、再生後は観光資源としてだけでなく、地元の歴史教育やまち歩きの目的地として受け止められている。[奈良市ホームページ](https://www.city.nara.lg.jp/site/bunkazai/6912.html), [旧奈良監獄アーカイブス](https://hoshinoresorts.com/nara-prison-museum/research-info/ja/history/turning-point/)

deepdive.photo_tips: 正面の赤レンガ外観は午前の順光、放射状の全景は少し離れた位置から広角で。中庭や扇形構造は高低差を入れると映える。保存・展示エリアは指示に従い、撮影禁止表示のある室内は撮らない。

deepdive.warnings_extra: 保存・展示エリアでは係員の案内に従い、立入制限や撮影禁止表示を守ること。旧刑務所だった場所として静粛に見学し、居住地域に近いので大声や無断の敷地外撮影は避ける。

deepdive.history_jp_en: The Former Nara Prison is a modern prison building that began renovation planning in 1901 (Meiji 34) as part of the Meiji government's drive to internationalize prison standards, and was completed in 1908 (Meiji 41). It was designed by Yamashita Keijiro, a judicial engineer, using the "Haviland system" in which cell blocks radiate outward from a central guard post. Tracing the lineage of the Edo-period Nara magistrate's office and the Nara Prison, it opened at its present site in 1909 (Meiji 42), was renamed Nara Juvenile Prison in 1946 (Showa 21), and closed in 2017 (Heisei 29). As one of the Five Great Meiji-Era Prisons and the only one where the full complement of main buildings survives intact, it was designated an Important Cultural Property on February 23, 2017. [Former Nara Prison Archives](https://hoshinoresorts.com/nara-prison-museum/research-info/ja/history/), [Nara City official website](https://www.city.nara.lg.jp/site/bunkazai/6912.html), [The Five Great Meiji-Era Prisons](https://hoshinoresorts.com/nara-prison-museum/research-info/ja/history/meiji-five-prison/)
deepdive.cultural_context_jp_en: The facility was born as a place where the modern state shifted its penal philosophy from "punishment" to "correction," placing emphasis on hygiene, surveillance, and classification. The radial layout symbolizes the rationalization of inmate management, while the red brick and Western architectural style symbolize the modernization of the judicial system. Today it is reinterpreted as a learning resource that spans architectural history, the history of punishment, and regional tourism, while preserving a difficult heritage. [Former Nara Prison Archives](https://hoshinoresorts.com/nara-prison-museum/research-info/ja/), [Nara Prison Museum official site](https://hoshinoresorts.com/nara-prison-museum/ja/), [Ministry of Justice PDF](https://www.moj.go.jp/content/001225663.pdf)
deepdive.local_perspective_jp_en: Nara City has conducted tours and explanations of plans for preservation and utilization with the site's cultural property value as a given. Even after closure, there has been strong interest in the facility as a site conveying "the memory of local modernization," and after its renovation it has been received not only as a tourism resource but also as a destination for local history education and town walks. [Nara City official website](https://www.city.nara.lg.jp/site/bunkazai/6912.html), [Former Nara Prison Archives](https://hoshinoresorts.com/nara-prison-museum/research-info/ja/history/turning-point/)

- Book/report: Characteristics and Background of the Former Nara Prison Preservation and Utilization Project (Noda Research Institute series materials, 2023) — summarizes the history of preservation and utilization.
- TV/media: "Japan's Oldest Prison Becomes a Museum" (ABC Television, 2026) — opening coverage introducing the interior of the facility.

deepdive.best_visit_time_en: Morning in spring or autumn. Light reaches the red brickwork easily and a weekday that combines well with Nara Park tourism is recommended.
deepdive.photo_tips_en: The red-brick exterior at the front is best photographed in morning front-lighting; the full radial plan is effective from a slightly distant position with a wide-angle lens. Including the elevation change of the courtyard and fan-shaped structure adds visual interest. Follow instructions in preservation and exhibition areas; do not photograph inside rooms where photography is prohibited.
deepdive.trivia_en:
- Of the Five Great Meiji-Era Prisons, the only one where the full complement of main buildings survives is the Former Nara Prison.
- The designer, Yamashita Keijiro, was a Ministry of Justice engineer known not only for prison buildings but also for courthouse architecture.
- After closing in 2017 it became a leading example of "preservation and utilization" through conversion into a heritage hotel and museum.
deepdive.warnings_extra_en: In preservation and exhibition areas, follow staff guidance and observe access restrictions and photography prohibition signs. Visit quietly in keeping with the site's former function as a prison, and as it is near a residential area, avoid loud voices and unauthorized photography from outside the grounds.

name: 信楽巨大狸群
name_kana: しがらききょだいたぬきぐん
address: 〒529-1851 滋賀県甲賀市信楽町牧1293-2（信楽陶苑たぬき村）
fee: 入場無料（陶芸体験は別途）
summary: 信楽焼の名産地・滋賀県甲賀市信楽町は、全国に信楽狸（ぽんぽこたぬき）を普及させた「狸の聖地」。駅に降り立った瞬間から無数の狸がお出迎えし、町全体が狸に占領されている。「たぬき村」では巨大狸から超迷彩カラーの奇抜な狸まで多様な狸が並び、「信楽焼狸の不動の笑い顔」と大量陳列が作り出すカオス感が最高。信楽高原鐵道という「ローカル線鉄道体験」つきで来られる。
highlights: 信楽駅を降りた瞬間から始まる「全方位たぬき包囲網」
たぬき村の「大・中・小・奇抜な狸の大量陳列」のカオス
焼き物体験で「自分だけの狸」を作るという体験
from_kameyama: 車で約45分（名阪国道→国道307号）

deepdive.history_jp: 信楽の狸像は、信楽焼の長い陶業史のなかでは比較的新しく、成立は昭和前期、一般には1900年頃〜1930年代初頭とされる。生みの親は初代「狸庵」藤原銕造とされ、京都で試作した狸を信楽に移して独自の定型を広めたという説が有力である。昭和26年（1951）の昭和天皇行幸の際、沿道に並べた狸像が報道され、全国的な知名度が一気に高まった。甲賀市公式も、信楽駅前の巨大狸を町の代表的記念撮影スポットとして紹介している。信楽町観光協会によれば駅前大たぬきは昭和62年（1987）設置で、町の玄関口を象徴する存在である。[旅する、千年](https://sixancientkilns.jp/shigaraki/), [甲賀市公式](https://www.city.koka.lg.jp/item/9426.htm), [信楽町観光協会](https://www.e-shigaraki.org/special-recommendation/ootanuki.html)
deepdive.cultural_context_jp: 信楽狸は、商売繁盛や家内安全を願う日本の縁起物文化と、信楽焼の産地アイデンティティが結びついて生まれた。八相縁起という解釈が後から整えられ、置物が「意味を持つ工芸品」として普及したことで、土産物を超えて地域の象徴になった。巨大狸の群立は、観光資源であると同時に、町が自らの焼き物文化を可視化する地域表象でもある。[旅する、千年](https://sixancientkilns.jp/shigaraki/), [Government of Japan](https://www.gov-online.go.jp/hlj/ja/march_2026/march_2026-03.html)
deepdive.local_perspective_jp: 地元では、駅前大たぬきや町内の狸群は「信楽らしさ」を示す看板役として親しまれている。信楽町観光協会は季節ごとに衣装替えを行い、駅前の狸を町のランドマークとして維持している。観光客を迎える一方、地元の人にとっても日常の風景であり、町の誇りとして扱われている。[信楽町観光協会](https://www.e-shigaraki.org/special-recommendation/ootanuki.html)

deepdive.photo_tips: 信楽駅前は正面からの全景、たぬき村は巨大狸の足元から見上げる構図が定番。青空の順光で表情と釉薬感が出やすい。私有地内は案内に従い、施設の撮影ルールを確認。

- 信楽駅前大たぬきは昭和62年（1987）設置で、公衆電話機能を持つランドマークだった。

deepdive.warnings_extra: 駅前や店先の狸は観光用でも、商売や地域の象徴として大切にされている。無断で登ったり触れたりせず、私有地では施設の指示に従うこと。人や車の通行を妨げないよう配慮したい。

deepdive.history_jp_en: The tanuki (raccoon dog) figurines of Shigaraki are relatively recent within the long pottery history of Shigaraki ware; their establishment is generally dated to around 1900 to the early 1930s. The creator is widely attributed to the first generation "Tanuki-an" Fujiwara Tetsuzo, who is said to have moved prototypes he tested in Kyoto to Shigaraki and spread a distinctive standard form there. When Emperor Showa visited the area in 1951 (Showa 26), the tanuki figurines lined along the roadway were covered by media reports and their popularity skyrocketed nationwide. Koka City's official website also introduces the large tanuki in front of Shigaraki Station as the town's representative commemorative photo spot. According to the Shigaraki Town Tourism Association, the large tanuki in front of the station was installed in 1987 (Showa 62) and is a landmark that symbolizes the gateway to the town. [Traveling through a Thousand Years](https://sixancientkilns.jp/shigaraki/), [Koka City official site](https://www.city.koka.lg.jp/item/9426.htm), [Shigaraki Town Tourism Association](https://www.e-shigaraki.org/special-recommendation/ootanuki.html)
deepdive.cultural_context_jp_en: The Shigaraki tanuki emerged from the convergence of Japan's lucky-charm culture — praying for prosperity in business and domestic harmony — and the producer identity of Shigaraki ware's area of origin. The Hassō Engi (eight-fold good fortune) interpretation was developed afterward, and as figurines spread as "craftwork with meaning" they transcended the status of souvenir to become a regional symbol. The cluster of oversized tanuki statues is simultaneously a tourism resource and a local visual representation through which the town makes its pottery culture visible. [Traveling through a Thousand Years](https://sixancientkilns.jp/shigaraki/), [Government of Japan / HIGHLIGHTING Japan](https://www.gov-online.go.jp/hlj/ja/march_2026/march_2026-03.html)
deepdive.local_perspective_jp_en: Locally, the large tanuki in front of the station and the clusters of tanuki around town are cherished as the "face of Shigaraki." The Shigaraki Town Tourism Association changes the figurines' costumes seasonally and maintains the station-front tanuki as the town's landmark. While welcoming tourists, for local residents the figurines are also an everyday landscape and a source of local pride. [Shigaraki Town Tourism Association](https://www.e-shigaraki.org/special-recommendation/ootanuki.html)

deepdive.best_visit_time_en: A sunny morning just after arriving on the Shigaraki Kogen Railway. Morning front-lighting is recommended for photographing the large station-front tanuki and the clusters around town.
deepdive.photo_tips_en: A full frontal shot of the Shigaraki Station plaza, and a composition looking up from the base of the giant tanuki at Tanuki Mura, are standard approaches. Direct sunlight from the front makes the figurines' expressions and glaze texture stand out. Follow guidance when in private property, and confirm photography rules at each facility.
deepdive.trivia_en:
- The tanuki figurines are said to represent eight kinds of good fortune through the "Hassō Engi," a system of meaning that was developed and standardized after the fact.
- The large tanuki in front of Shigaraki Station was installed in 1987 (Showa 62) and was once a landmark with a public telephone function.
- The nationwide spread of tanuki culture was greatly triggered by media coverage of Emperor Showa's visit in 1951.
deepdive.warnings_extra_en: The tanuki statues in front of the station and outside shops are cherished as symbols of commerce and community, even as tourist objects. Please do not climb on or touch them without permission. Follow facility instructions on private property. Please take care not to obstruct the passage of people and vehicles.

name: 花の窟神社
name_kana: はなのいわやじんじゃ
address: 〒519-4325 三重県熊野市有馬町130
summary: 日本書紀にも登場する、日本最古とも言われる神社。高さ45mの巨岩「花の窟」をそのままご神体とし、社殿が一切存在しない。神話上、火の神・軻遇突智（カグツチ）を産んで亡くなったイザナミが葬られた場所とされる。年2回（2月2日・10月2日）の例大祭ではカラフルな布を岩と舞台の間に渡す「お綱かけ神事」が行われ、古代の信仰形態がそのまま現代に残る。2004年世界遺産登録。
highlights: 「社殿ゼロ」という日本最古の信仰形態が2,000年以上続く
45mの巨岩がそのまま神様という圧倒的スケール感
日本神話の「イザナミの墓」という設定の重さ
from_kameyama: 車で約1時間40分（紀勢道経由）

deepdive.history_jp: 花の窟神社は、720年（奈良時代）成立の『日本書紀』神代巻に、伊弉冉尊（イザナミ）が火の神・軻遇突智を産んで死に、「紀伊国熊野の有馬村」に葬られたと記される伝承地に比定される。熊野市公式は、この地を「国産みの舞台」としての古代の聖地と位置づけ、花を供えて祀ったことが社号の由来と伝える。現地は古来、社殿を持たず高さ約45mの巨岩そのものを御神体とする磐座信仰の場で、花を飾り祀る原始的祭祀の姿を今に伝える。明治期に神社として整理される以前は、墓所・御陵として語られてきたこともあり、神話・民俗・地域記憶が重なる場所である。[熊野市公式](https://www.city.kumano.lg.jp/tourism/?content=191), [熊野市VR](https://www.city.kumano.lg.jp/vr/hananoiwaya/index.php), [熊野古道・熊野市観光](https://kumano-kankou.com/?p=14), [Wikipedia](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E8%8A%B1%E7%AA%9F%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE)
deepdive.cultural_context_jp: 社殿を置かず巨岩を神体とする形は、山・岩・海に霊威を見いだす熊野の自然信仰の古層を示す。熊野市観光は、ここを熊野三山以前の古代信仰に連なる重要地と説明し、世界遺産登録後は参詣・観光の両面で「熊野に来た」と実感させる象徴になった。2月2日・10月2日の例大祭とお綱かけ神事は、共同体が神と結び直す年中行事として、現在も地域アイデンティティを支えている。[熊野市公式](https://www.city.kumano.lg.jp/tourism/?content=191), [三重県文化観光](https://www.bunka.pref.mie.lg.jp/646580347590022.htm)
deepdive.local_perspective_jp: 熊野市の案内では、お綱かけ神事は地元の人々が綯った大綱を掛け替える行事で、三重県の無形民俗文化財にも指定されている。地元にとっては単なる観光名所ではなく、毎年の祭礼で共同作業と祈りを継承する場として扱われている。[熊野市公式](https://www.city.kumano.lg.jp/vr/hananoiwaya/index.php), [熊野市文化財一覧](https://www.city.kumano.lg.jp/tourism/?content=57)
deepdive.related_works:
- 『日本書紀』神代巻（720年）— 伊弉冉尊の葬地として紀伊国熊野有馬村を記述
- 『紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道』世界遺産登録（UNESCO、2004年）— 熊野参詣道伊勢路の構成資産として花の窟を含む
- 『お綱かけ神事・花の窟神社』(映像作品/三重県・番組紹介、年不詳) — 祭礼の民俗的継承を記録
- 大谷翔平選手の参拝がテレビ・ネット記事で紹介（各種報道、年不詳）

deepdive.best_visit_time: 例大祭の2月2日か10月2日、できれば神事開始前の午前中。
deepdive.photo_tips: 巨岩全景は参道入口側から社殿のない構図で撮ると特徴が出る。お綱かけ神事の日は綱の張り込みを遠景で。拝所付近は参拝者優先で、柵内や神事の進行を妨げる撮影は避ける。
deepdive.trivia:
- 巨岩がそのまま御神体で、社殿を持たないため、古代の磐座信仰を体感できる。
- 例大祭のお綱かけ神事は約170mの大綱を掛け替える壮大な行事として知られる。
- 花を供えて祀ったことが社号の由来とされ、名称自体が信仰の痕跡を残している。
deepdive.warnings_extra: 巨岩は信仰対象なので、柵越しでも不用意に触れず、参拝者の流れを妨げないこと。神事中は係員の指示に従い、フラッシュや長時間の場所取りは控える。

deepdive.history_jp_en: Hana-no-Iwaya Jinja is identified as the traditional site where, according to the divine age section of the Nihon Shoki (compiled 720 CE in the Nara period), Izanami-no-Mikoto died giving birth to the fire deity Kagutsuchi and was buried in "Arima Village, Kumano, Kii Province." The official Kumano City website positions this site as an ancient sacred place "at the heart of the world-creation narrative" and states that the shrine name derives from the custom of offering flowers in worship. The site has since antiquity maintained no shrine buildings, and the approximately 45-meter-high boulder itself is the shintai (sacred object), making it a place of iwakura (sacred rock) veneration that conveys the form of primeval ritual worship of flowers and adornment. Before being organized as a shrine in the Meiji period, the site was also described as a grave or imperial mausoleum, and it is a place where myth, folklore, and local memory overlap. [Kumano City official website](https://www.city.kumano.lg.jp/tourism/?content=191), [Kumano City VR](https://www.city.kumano.lg.jp/vr/hananoiwaya/index.php), [Kumano Kodo — Kumano City Tourism](https://kumano-kankou.com/?p=14), [Wikipedia](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E8%8A%B1%E7%AA%9F%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE)
deepdive.cultural_context_jp_en: The form of venerating a giant boulder without shrine buildings indicates the ancient stratum of Kumano's nature-based belief, which perceives spiritual power in mountains, rocks, and the sea. Kumano City's tourism materials explain this as an important site connected to ancient belief predating the Kumano Sanzan (Three Grand Shrines of Kumano), and since the UNESCO World Heritage inscription it has become a symbol that makes visitors feel they have truly arrived in Kumano — in both pilgrimage and tourist terms. The grand festival (reitaisai) on February 2 and October 2 and the Otsunakake Shinji (rope-hanging Shinto rite) continue today as an annual observance through which the community renews its bond with the deity, sustaining local identity. [Kumano City official website](https://www.city.kumano.lg.jp/tourism/?content=191), [Mie Prefecture Cultural Tourism](https://www.bunka.pref.mie.lg.jp/646580347590022.htm)
deepdive.local_perspective_jp_en: In Kumano City's description, the Otsunakake Shinji is an event in which local people replace the large rope they have braided themselves, and it is also designated a Prefecturally Designated Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Mie Prefecture. For the local community it is not merely a tourist attraction but a venue for joint labor and prayer transmitted through annual festival rites. [Kumano City official website](https://www.city.kumano.lg.jp/vr/hananoiwaya/index.php), [Kumano City Cultural Property List](https://www.city.kumano.lg.jp/tourism/?content=57)
deepdive.related_works_en:
- Nihon Shoki (Divine Age section) (720 CE) — describes Arima Village, Kumano, Kii Province as the burial place of Izanami-no-Mikoto
- Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range (UNESCO World Heritage inscription, 2004) — Hana-no-Iwaya is included as a component site of the Kumano Sankeimichi Ise-ji route
- "Otsunakake Shinji — Hana-no-Iwaya Jinja" (audiovisual work / Mie Prefecture program introduction, year unconfirmed) — documents the folkloric transmission of the festival
- Otani Shohei's visit was covered in television and internet articles (various media, year unconfirmed)

deepdive.best_visit_time_en: The grand festival on February 2 or October 2, preferably the morning before the ritual begins.
deepdive.photo_tips_en: The full view of the giant boulder is best captured from the approach entrance side in a composition without shrine buildings, which highlights the site's distinctive character. On the day of the Otsunakake Shinji, photograph the rope-hanging process from a distance. Give priority to worshippers near the worship area, and avoid photography that obstructs the area within the fence or the progress of the ritual.
deepdive.trivia_en:
- The giant boulder itself is the shintai (sacred object) and there are no shrine buildings, making it possible to experience ancient iwakura (sacred rock) veneration directly.
- The Otsunakake Shinji at the grand festival is known as a magnificent event in which an approximately 170-meter rope is replaced.
- The shrine name is said to derive from the custom of offering flowers in worship, meaning the name itself preserves traces of the act of faith.
deepdive.warnings_extra_en: As the giant boulder is an object of veneration, please do not touch it carelessly even from behind a fence, and do not obstruct the flow of worshippers. During Shinto rites, follow staff instructions and refrain from flash photography or prolonged occupation of a spot.

name: 二見興玉神社・夫婦岩
name_kana: ふたみおきたまじんじゃ
address: 〒519-0602 三重県伊勢市二見町江575
summary: 伊勢神宮参拝前に行う禊（みそぎ）の場として古代から続く神社。しめ縄で結ばれた大小2つの岩（夫婦岩）は、沖合700mの海中に沈む霊石「興玉神石」と太陽を拝む鳥居の役割を担う。境内には無数のカエル像が奉納されており、その異様な密度は「カエル地獄」と呼ばれる。夏至の前後には二つの岩の間から日の出が昇り、古代人が「太陽の死と再生」を祈った場所であることを実感させる。
highlights: しめ縄で結ばれた海の大岩という「生きた神話の鳥居」
カエル像が境内を埋め尽くす異様な「カエル地獄」
夏至・冬至の「岩の間からの日の出・月の出」は絶景
from_kameyama: 車で約50分（亀山IC→伊勢道）

deepdive.history_jp: 二見興玉神社は、社名の通り「興玉石（御膳岩）」を本体とする古い霊地で、公式サイトは「古来より興玉石・御膳岩と称せられ」たとし、猿田彦大神が皇大神の御神幸を迎えた神蹟に由来すると伝える[二見興玉神社 公式](https://futamiokitamajinja.or.jp/meguru/%E8%88%88%E7%8E%89%E7%A5%9E%E7%9F%B3/)。現在の神社は、天平年間（729〜748年）に行基が江寺を創建し境内に興玉社を建てたという伝承、さらに明治9年（1876年）の神仏分離後に興玉社と三宮神社（三狐神社）を合わせ、明治43年（1910年）に二見興玉神社へ改称したという近代社史が案内動画等で語られている[YouTube「二見興玉神社/三重県伊勢市【夫婦岩】…」](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Rge7xAA1je0)。また、伊勢湾の舟人が航海の守護として深く崇敬したとも公式は記す[二見興玉神社 公式](https://futamiokitamajinja.or.jp/meguru/%E8%88%88%E7%8E%89%E7%A5%9E%E7%9F%B3/)。
deepdive.cultural_context_jp: 二見は伊勢神宮参拝の前に身を清める「禊の地」で、海と朝日、夫婦岩を結ぶ構図そのものが、境界を越えるための宗教的装置として働いてきた[二見興玉神社 公式](https://futamiokitamajinja.or.jp/)、[三重県 文化の道](https://www.bunka.pref.mie.lg.jp/kaidou/walking/pdf/ise_all.pdf)。夫婦岩は興玉神石を遥拝する鳥居の役目を担い、夏至前後の朝日信仰を可視化するため、海辺の景勝と民間信仰が結びついた場所として現代まで受け継がれている[二見興玉神社 公式](https://futamiokitamajinja.or.jp/meguru/meotoiwa/)。
deepdive.local_perspective_jp: 公式案内や訪問記では、二見は「伊勢参りは二見から」として早朝参拝が重視され、地元では観光地であると同時に、今も禊と祈りの場として扱われていることがうかがえる[二見興玉神社 公式](https://futamiokitamajinja.or.jp/)、[note「伊勢旅行2日目①二見興玉神社・早朝参拝」](https://note.com/fumika3939/n/nca9d903d1fb1)。境内のカエル像も、無事帰る・若返る・お金が返るという縁起担ぎとして親しまれている[三重県教材PDF](https://www.pref.mie.lg.jp/common/content/000772066.pdf)。

- 『大初日 二見の巌を 抱擁す』青畝石碑（富安風生/松本青畝、参拝詠、年代は公式未記載）[二見興玉神社 公式](https://futamiokitamajinja.or.jp/meguru/seihosekihi/)

deepdive.best_visit_time: 夏至前後の5〜7月、日の出直後の早朝。特に夏至当日の朝が最良。
deepdive.photo_tips: 夫婦岩は日の出方向を正面に、二つの岩と注連縄を一枚に収めるのが定番。朝は逆光気味なので、日の出前の青い時間か、岩のシルエットを活かす構図がよい。境内は通常撮影可だが、参拝者の邪魔は避ける。
deepdive.trivia:
- 夫婦岩の中央から昇る朝日は、夏至を中心に5〜7月が最も美しいと公式が案内する。
- 境内のカエルは「無事帰る」「若返る」「お金が返る」の験担ぎで増えたとされる。
- 興玉神石は今は海中の暗礁だが、かつては露出していたと公式が説明する。
deepdive.warnings_extra: 神社は禊と遥拝の場なので、岩や注連縄に触れすぎない。早朝は参拝者が多く、撮影時は順番と足元に配慮する。拝礼は二拝二拍手一拝を基本に、静かに参拝する。
deepdive.sources: [二見興玉神社 公式サイト](https://futamiokitamajinja.or.jp/), [夫婦岩の公式案内](https://futamiokitamajinja.or.jp/meguru/meotoiwa/), [興玉神石の公式案内](https://futamiokitamajinja.or.jp/meguru/%E8%88%88%E7%8E%89%E7%A5%9E%E7%9F%B3/), [三重県教材PDF](https://www.pref.mie.lg.jp/common/content/000772066.pdf), [三重県「伊勢街道」PDF](https://www.bunka.pref.mie.lg.jp/kaidou/walking/pdf/ise_all.pdf)
deepdive.history_jp_en: Futami Okitama Jinja, as its name indicates, is an ancient sacred site centered on the "Okitama-ishi (Omiwa-iwa)" (the sacred rock). The official website states it was "known as Okitama-ishi or Omiwa-iwa since ancient times" and traces its origin to the sacred trace where Sarutahiko Okami awaited the divine procession of the Great Deity of Ise. [Futami Okitama Jinja official website](https://futamiokitamajinja.or.jp/meguru/%E8%88%88%E7%8E%89%E7%A5%9E%E7%9F%B3/) The history of the present shrine — including the tradition that Gyoki founded Edo-dera (Kotera) in the Tenpyo era (729–748 CE) and built an Okitama shrine within its precinct, the separation of Buddhism and Shinto in Meiji 9 (1876) after which the Okitama Shrine and the Sannomiya Shrine (Sankoji Shrine) were merged, and the renaming to Futami Okitama Jinja in Meiji 43 (1910) — is recounted in explanatory videos and similar sources. [YouTube "Futami Okitama Jinja / Ise City, Mie [Meoto-iwa]..."](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Rge7xAA1je0) The official website also notes that maritime people of Ise Bay venerated the shrine deeply as a guardian of seafaring. [Futami Okitama Jinja official website](https://futamiokitamajinja.or.jp/meguru/%E8%88%88%E7%8E%89%E7%A5%9E%E7%9F%B3/)
deepdive.cultural_context_jp_en: Futami functioned as a "place of misogi (ritual purification)" before visiting Ise Jingu, and the composition linking sea, sunrise, and the Meoto-iwa (Wedded Rocks) has operated as a religious device for crossing a threshold. [Futami Okitama Jinja official website](https://futamiokitamajinja.or.jp/), [Mie Prefecture Cultural Routes](https://www.bunka.pref.mie.lg.jp/kaidou/walking/pdf/ise_all.pdf) The Meoto-iwa (Wedded Rocks) serve as a torii gate for venerating the Okitama sacred rock from afar, and as a site that visualizes sunrise veneration centered on the summer solstice, it continues to this day as a convergence of coastal scenery and folk belief. [Futami Okitama Jinja official website](https://futamiokitamajinja.or.jp/meguru/meotoiwa/)
deepdive.local_perspective_jp_en: In official materials and visitor accounts, the saying "Ise pilgrimage begins at Futami" means early-morning visits are particularly emphasized, and it can be seen that locally the site is treated both as a tourist destination and as a place of purification and prayer to this day. [Futami Okitama Jinja official website](https://futamiokitamajinja.or.jp/), [note "Ise Trip Day 2 (1) Futami Okitama Jinja — Early Morning Visit"](https://note.com/fumika3939/n/nca9d903d1fb1) The frog statues in the precinct are also cherished as auspicious tokens — "buji kaeru (return safely)," "wakagaeru (rejuvenate)," and "okane ga kaeru (money returns)." [Mie Prefecture educational PDF](https://www.pref.mie.lg.jp/common/content/000772066.pdf)
deepdive.related_works_en:
- Stone monument of haiku by Yamaguchi Seishi: "Hatsu Fuji no / Torii to mo naru / Meoto-iwa" (Yamaguchi Seishi, composed during a New Year visit in 1987) [Futami Okitama Jinja official website](https://futamiokitamajinja.or.jp/meguru/seishisekihi/)
- Stone monument haiku attributed to Tomiyasu Fusei/Matsumoto Seiho: "Ohatsuka / Futami no iwa o / Hoyo su" (date not recorded on official site) [Futami Okitama Jinja official website](https://futamiokitamajinja.or.jp/meguru/seihosekihi/)
- Article on Omiwa-mochi (rice cakes): (Wikipedia, Japanese edition, described as originating with the deity enshrined in the "Ama-no-Iwaya" at Futami Okitama Jinja) [Wikipedia "Omiwa-mochi"](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%BE%A1%E7%A6%8F%E9%A4%85)
- Article on Meoto-iwa: (Wikipedia, Japanese edition, overview as a scenic spot) [Wikipedia "Meoto-iwa"](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%A4%AB%E5%A9%A6%E5%B2%A9)

deepdive.best_visit_time_en: May to July around the summer solstice, early morning just after sunrise. The morning of the summer solstice itself is the finest.
deepdive.photo_tips_en: Facing the direction of sunrise, composing both rocks and the straw rope (shimenawa) in a single frame is standard. In the morning the light tends toward backlight, so the blue hour before sunrise or a silhouette composition making use of the rock forms works well. Photography is generally permitted throughout the precinct but should not disturb worshippers.
deepdive.trivia_en:
- The official site states that the sunrise framed between the Meoto-iwa is at its most beautiful in May–July, centered on the summer solstice.
- The frog statues in the precinct are said to have multiplied as good-luck charms for "returning safely (buji kaeru)," "rejuvenating (wakagaeru)," and "money returning (okane ga kaeru)."
- The Okitama sacred rock is now a submerged reef, but the official site explains that it was once exposed above water.
deepdive.warnings_extra_en: As the shrine is a place of misogi and distant worship, please refrain from touching the rocks and shimenawa excessively. Early mornings bring many worshippers; take turns politely and mind your footing when photographing. As the standard form of worship, practice two bows, two claps, one bow (nire ni-haiden ichirei) and worship quietly.

name: 旧女鬼トンネル
name_kana: きゅうめきとんねる
address: 三重県多気郡多気町女鬼周辺
summary: 三重県随一の心霊スポットと称されるトンネル。苔むした石造りの入口から漂う冷気と、「女性の霊が車に乗り込む」「トンネル内でエンジンが止まる」という噂が絶えない。名前自体が「女鬼」という強烈さで、地元でも怖れられている。現在は立入禁止で来訪は強く非推奨。歴史的にも謎が多く、心霊系コンテンツでは定番の取り上げられ方をする三重のシンボル的心霊スポット。トンネル周辺の廃集落跡が雰囲気をさらに高める。
highlights: 「女鬼」という地名・名称が持つ民俗的な重み
石造りのトンネルが発する物理的な不気味さ
心霊スポットランキングで常に三重No.1に挙がる知名度
from_kameyama: 車で約30分

deepdive.history_jp: 旧女鬼トンネルの正式名称は女鬼隧道で、三重県多気郡多気町の県道119号松阪度会線にある。Wikipediaによれば、女鬼峠は熊野古道伊勢路の最初の難所で、江戸時代以前から往来があり、峠南側には1738年（元文3年）に如意輪観音の石仏が置かれた。現トンネルは1934年（昭和9年）に開通し、当時の三重県知事・早川三郎の筆の扁額が掲げられたとされる。1996年（平成8年）12月に新女鬼トンネルが開通して旧道化し、現在は両側に鉄扉が設けられて通り抜けできない。心霊由来の由緒は複数の噂にすぎず、女性の霊や人柱伝説が語られるが、史実としては確認できない。([Wikipedia](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%A5%B3%E9%AC%BC%E3%83%88%E3%83%B3%E3%83%8D%E3%83%AB))
deepdive.cultural_context_jp: 女鬼峠は伊勢路の難所として旅人の信仰・供養・道中安全の対象になり、如意輪観音や地蔵、道標が残る峠景観は、熊野古道の「越える道」の記憶を伝える。心霊スポット化は、旧道・廃隧道・閉鎖空間が持つ不気味さに、峠の死と再生の民俗的想像力が重なった結果とみられる。現在は観光・保全の文脈でも語られ、地域史の入口としての意味を持つ。([Wikipedia](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%A5%B3%E9%AC%BC%E3%83%88%E3%83%B3%E3%83%8D%E3%83%AB), [FC2](https://sanaemac.blog.fc2.com/blog-entry-242.html))
deepdive.local_perspective_jp: ブログでは、旧トンネルは新トンネルの脇にあり道路も閉鎖され、徒歩で近づく場所として記録されている。地域側では危険な旧道というより、熊野古道の一部として案内板や整備が進み、峠や周辺の史跡を歩く対象として扱われている様子がうかがえる。心霊の話は広く流通するが、地元では歴史景観の一部として静かに見られている。([Ameblo](https://ameblo.jp/quicknick/entry-12450871092.html), [FC2](https://sanaemac.blog.fc2.com/blog-entry-242.html))

[【心霊探訪No.96】旧女鬼トンネル](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O_Apq7OgmYI)
deepdive.best_visit_time: 立入禁止のため訪問非推奨。記録目的なら昼間の晴天時に新女鬼トンネル周辺の公道から外観確認のみ。
deepdive.photo_tips: 撮影は新女鬼トンネル側の公道から外観を遠景で。旧隧道は閉鎖され立入不可なので、扉や敷地内への接近・侵入は避ける。薄曇りよりも日中の順光で石積みや苔の質感が出やすい。
deepdive.trivia:
- 女鬼峠は江戸時代には「祢き峠」「ねぎ峠」とも呼ばれた。([Wikipedia](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%A5%B3%E9%AC%BC%E3%83%88%E3%83%B3%E3%83%8D%E3%83%AB))
- 峠には1738年（元文3年）の如意輪観音石仏があり、旅の安全祈願の性格を持つ。([Wikipedia](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%A5%B3%E9%AC%BC%E3%83%88%E3%83%B3%E3%83%8D%E3%83%AB))
- 旧トンネルは「女性の霊」「車が止まる」といった噂で有名だが、これらは心霊系の伝承として扱うべきで史実未確認。
deepdive.warnings_extra: 旧女鬼トンネルは立入禁止で、現地接近や夜間の撮影は避ける。周辺は熊野古道の歴史景観なので、騒音・無断駐車・私有地侵入は厳禁。心霊目的の迷惑行為ではなく、文化財周辺として静かに扱う。

deepdive.history_jp_en: The formal name of the Old Onigajo Tunnel is Onigoroshi Tunnel (Onigoroshi Zuido), located on Mie Prefectural Road 119 (Matsusaka-Watarai Line) in Taki Town, Taki County, Mie Prefecture. According to Wikipedia, Onigajo Pass was the first difficult section on the Kumano Kodo Ise-ji route; traffic passed through it before the Edo period, and a stone Buddha of the Nyoirin Kannon was placed on the southern side of the pass in 1738 (Genbun 3). The current tunnel opened in 1934 (Showa 9), and its tympanum was inscribed with calligraphy by Hayakawa Saburo, the then-Governor of Mie Prefecture. In December 1996 (Heisei 8), a new Onigajo Tunnel opened, rendering the old road disused; at present both ends are equipped with iron gates and the tunnel cannot be passed through. The supernatural associations derive solely from multiple rumors; stories of a female supernatural apparition and a legend of human sacrifice offered during construction are told, but none can be verified as historical fact. ([Wikipedia](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%A5%B3%E9%AC%BC%E3%83%88%E3%83%B3%E3%83%8D%E3%83%AB))
deepdive.cultural_context_jp_en: As a difficult section of the Ise-ji route, Onigajo Pass became an object of travelers' faith, memorial rites, and prayers for safe passage; the pass landscape with its surviving Nyoirin Kannon, Jizo, and road markers conveys the memory of the Kumano Kodo as a "road to cross." The transformation into a site associated with supernatural phenomena appears to be the result of the eeriness inherent in an old road, an abandoned tunnel, and an enclosed space converging with the folkloric imagination of death and regeneration at a mountain pass. Today it is discussed in both tourism and preservation contexts and holds significance as an entry point into local history. ([Wikipedia](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%A5%B3%E9%AC%BC%E3%83%88%E3%83%B3%E3%83%8D%E3%83%AB), [FC2](https://sanaemac.blog.fc2.com/blog-entry-242.html))
deepdive.local_perspective_jp_en: Blog accounts record the old tunnel as located beside the new tunnel, with the road closed, approachable only on foot. On the community side, signboards and infrastructure have been developed not as a dangerous old road but as part of the Kumano Kodo, and it appears that the pass and surrounding historical sites are treated as objects for walking. Stories of supernatural phenomena circulate widely, but locally the site is viewed quietly as part of the historic landscape. ([Ameblo](https://ameblo.jp/quicknick/entry-12450871092.html), [FC2](https://sanaemac.blog.fc2.com/blog-entry-242.html))

deepdive.best_visit_time_en: Not recommended for visits as it is off-limits. For documentation purposes only, the exterior can be viewed from the public road around the new Onigajo Tunnel during daylight hours on a clear day.
deepdive.photo_tips_en: Photography from the public road on the new Onigajo Tunnel side, capturing the exterior from a distance, is recommended. The old tunnel is closed and off-limits, so avoid approaching or entering the gates or the grounds. Overcast light rather than midday direct sun brings out the texture of the stonework and moss more effectively.
deepdive.trivia_en:
- Onigajo Pass was also called "Negi Pass" or "Negi-toge" in the Edo period. ([Wikipedia](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%A5%B3%E9%AC%BC%E3%83%88%E3%83%B3%E3%83%8D%E3%83%AB))
- The pass has a stone Buddha of the Nyoirin Kannon from 1738 (Genbun 3), reflecting its character as a site for prayers for safe travel. ([Wikipedia](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%A5%B3%E9%AC%BC%E3%83%88%E3%83%B3%E3%83%8D%E3%83%AB))
- The old tunnel is famous for stories of "a female supernatural apparition" and "cars stalling," but these should be treated as supernatural folklore rather than historically verified accounts.
deepdive.warnings_extra_en: The old Onigajo Tunnel is off-limits; please do not approach on-site or attempt nighttime photography. As the surrounding area is the historic landscape of the Kumano Kodo, noise, unauthorized parking, and trespassing on private property are strictly prohibited. Treat the area as a cultural heritage site — not as a site for supernatural-themed misconduct — and behave quietly.

name: 旧長野トンネル周辺
name_kana: きゅうながのとんねる
address: 三重県津市美杉町・伊賀市方面（長野峠）
summary: 津市と伊賀市を結ぶ長野峠に存在する。明治・大正・昭和各時代のトンネルが並ぶという特異な場所で、「作業服姿の霊」「首のないライダー」の目撃が多数報告されている。時代の積み重なりが生み出した複合的な「怪異」の場所として知られる。旧道はほぼ廃道化しており、深い山中に取り残された状態。亀山市から比較的近く三重の心霊スポット代表格。
highlights: 3つの時代のトンネルが並ぶ唯一無二の地形
複数世代の霊が「混在する」という多層的な怪異
旧道廃道化による完全な「忘れられた場所」感
from_kameyama: 車で約30分

deepdive.history_jp: 長野峠は三重県津市と伊賀市の境にある国道163号旧道で、峠越えの難所を解消するために段階的にトンネルが掘られた。旧長野トンネル（初代）は1885年（明治18年）に完成し、長さは216mとされるが205mとする資料もある。伊賀側と伊勢側の住民が費用を出し合って開通したとされ、花崗岩製のアーチが特徴だった。1939年（昭和14年）にはほぼ真下に長野トンネル（二代目、約300m）が造られ、2008年7月12日には新長野トンネル（三代目、1,966m）が供用開始され、旧道区間は役目を終えた。旧長野トンネル自体は現在崩壊し通行不可で、周辺の廃道化も進んでいる。[長野峠 (三重県) - Wikipedia](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%95%B7%E9%87%8E%E5%B3%A0_(%E4%B8%89%E9%87%8D%E7%9C%8C)) [国道163号 - Wikipedia](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%9B%BD%E9%81%93163%E5%8F%B7)
deepdive.cultural_context_jp: 明治・昭和・平成の三世代トンネルが同じ峠に重なることで、近代道路史の「層」が可視化された場所である。廃道化した旧道は、生活道路の更新と引き換えに忘れられた空間でもあり、そこに事故や工事の記憶が重なって怪談化したと考えられる。現代では、土木遺産・廃道探訪・心霊スポットという複数の文脈で語られている。[長野峠 (三重県) - Wikipedia](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%95%B7%E9%87%8E%E5%B3%A0_(%E4%B8%89%E9%87%8D%E7%9C%8C))
deepdive.local_perspective_jp: 地元では「明治のトンネル」「昭和のトンネル」と呼び分けられ、生活のための峠道が新道へ移った結果、旧道は静かな遺構として扱われている。心霊的な噂はあるが、実見では廃道・危険地帯としての認識が強い。[長野峠 (三重県) - Wikipedia](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%95%B7%E9%87%8E%E5%B3%A0_(%E4%B8%89%E9%87%8C%E7%9C%8C))

deepdive.history_jp_en: Nagano Pass lies on the former Route 163 road straddling the boundary of Tsu City and Iga City, Mie Prefecture, and tunnels were progressively bored to overcome the difficulty of crossing the pass. The Old Nagano Tunnel (first generation) was completed in 1885 (Meiji 18) and is described as 216 meters long, although some sources give 205 meters. It is said to have been opened by contributions from residents on both the Iga and Ise sides, and was characterized by granite arches. In 1939 (Showa 14), a second-generation Nagano Tunnel (approximately 300 meters) was built almost directly beneath it, and on July 12, 2008, the New Nagano Tunnel (third generation, 1,966 meters) opened to traffic, ending the use of the old road section. The old Nagano Tunnel itself is now collapsed and impassable, and the surrounding area is increasingly becoming abandoned road. [Nagano Pass (Mie Prefecture) — Wikipedia](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%95%B7%E9%87%8E%E5%B3%A0_(%E4%B8%89%E9%87%8D%E7%9C%8C)), [National Route 163 — Wikipedia](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%9B%BD%E9%81%93163%E5%8F%B7)
deepdive.cultural_context_jp_en: By having Meiji-, Showa-, and Heisei-era tunnels layered at the same pass, this is a place where the "strata" of modern road history are made visible. The old road that has become an abandoned road is also a space forgotten in exchange for the renewal of an everyday thoroughfare, and it is thought that legends of accidents and construction work accumulated there to create ghost stories. Today it is discussed in multiple contexts: as civil engineering heritage, as an abandoned road to explore, and as a supernatural site. [Nagano Pass (Mie Prefecture) — Wikipedia](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%95%B7%E9%87%8E%E5%B3%A0_(%E4%B8%89%E9%87%8D%E7%9C%8C))
deepdive.local_perspective_jp_en: Locally the tunnels are distinguished as "the Meiji tunnel" and "the Showa tunnel," and as the everyday pass road moved to the new road, the old road is treated as a quiet ruin. There are stories of supernatural phenomena, but in actual observation the recognition of it as an abandoned road and danger zone is strong. [Nagano Pass (Mie Prefecture) — Wikipedia](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%95%B7%E9%87%8E%E5%B3%A0_(%E4%B8%89%E9%87%8C%E7%9C%8C))

deepdive.best_visit_time_en: Daytime during the fresh greenery season before summer. Only clear daytime conditions when the road surface is visible.
deepdive.photo_tips_en: Wide-angle shots of the old road entrance, the area around the Showa-era tunnel, and the stonework of the Meiji tunnel ruins. As the mountain shadows are deep and dark, morning angled light is advantageous. Do not photograph collapsed or off-limits sections.
deepdive.trivia_en:
- Three generations of tunnels — Meiji, Showa, and Heisei — are in close proximity, allowing comparison of the different eras in one place.
- It is said that the old Nagano Tunnel was opened with contributions from local residents.
- Famous as a supernatural site, but no primary source documentation of any paranormal history has been found.
deepdive.warnings_extra_en: As there are collapsed and impassable sections, unauthorized entry is strictly prohibited. As the area also has the character of a local thoroughfare, please avoid noise, parking, and littering; be considerate of surroundings when photographing.

name: 湯の山温泉廃墟群（杉屋旅館等）
name_kana: ゆのやまおんせんはいきょぐん
address: 三重県三重郡菰野町菰野8540（杉屋旅館）他
fee: 公式ホラーツアー参加（要事前申込）
hours: 特定ツアー開催日のみ
summary: 江戸元禄時代から続いた湯の山温泉の中でも最古の旅館「杉屋旅館」を含む廃墟群。温泉街の衰退により複数の旅館・ホテルが廃業・廃墟化し、かつての賑わいと現在の荒廃のコントラストが独特の空気を醸す。2025年にはホラーイベント会場として活用され「最恐心霊ツアー」が開催されるなど、廃墟の「観光資源化」が進んでいる先駆的事例。亀山市から車で約30分というアクセスも魅力。
highlights: 300年続いた旅館の廃墟という歴史の重み
心霊スポットとしての噂と、公式ホラーイベントという二面性
温泉街の観光衰退を如実に示す「消えた繁栄」
from_kameyama: 車で約30分

deepdive.history_jp: 湯の山温泉は、史料上は貞享4年（1687年）に8戸の湯屋が開かれたことが確認でき、江戸元禄期創業とされる杉屋旅館はその初期を代表する老舗の一つである。[三重県文化振興事業団](https://www.bunka.pref.mie.lg.jp/rekishi/kenshi/asp/meiji/detail496.html) によれば、温泉の起源には奈良時代・養老2年（718年）、淨薫和尚が薬師如来のお告げで発見したという伝承と、傷ついた鹿が湯で傷を癒した「鹿の湯」伝説がある。江戸期には菰野藩の保護のもと湯宿が整備され、湯の山の名は伊勢・北伊勢の湯治場として定着した。明治10年（1877年）の西南戦争後には傷病兵の臨時療養所が置かれ、療養効果が広く宣伝されて来遊者が増加した。杉屋旅館の創業年は元禄期（1688〜1704年）と紹介されることが多く、複数の訪問記では「湯の山で最古級の旅館」と説明される一方、解説サイトでは貞享4年（1687年）創業説も見られる。[湯の山温泉芸術祭「オンパク湯の山」](https://www.yunoyama-onsen-art.com/history.html)、[YOUよっかいち](https://www.you-yokkaichi.com/2025/11/10/41899/)、[廃屈な日々](https://haikutu.hatenablog.com/entry/2024/01/17/201228)
deepdive.cultural_context_jp: 湯の山温泉の廃墟群は、近代以降の温泉観光の隆盛と、バブル崩壊後の大型旅館の淘汰が重なって生まれた景観である。湯治と行楽の場として栄えた温泉街が、需要変化と建物老朽化で空洞化し、その痕跡が「廃墟の温泉街」として可視化された。現在は心霊・廃墟観光やイベント利用を通じ、衰退の記憶をどう共有するかが問われている。[三重県文化振興事業団](https://www.bunka.pref.mie.lg.jp/rekishi/kenshi/asp/meiji/detail496.html)、[YOUよっかいち](https://www.you-yokkaichi.com/2025/11/10/41899/)
deepdive.local_perspective_jp: 地元では長年、不法侵入や火災リスクを抱える厄介な景観として見られてきた一方、湯の山温泉協会関係者は「ツアー参加で無断侵入が減るなら」と静観の姿勢を示している。地域再生の文脈では、廃墟を壊すだけでなく、管理された形で資源化する試みとして受け止められている。[YOUよっかいち](https://www.you-yokkaichi.com/2025/11/10/41899/)、[東海テレビ](https://www.tokai-tv.com/tokainews/feature/article_20220401_17339)
deepdive.related_works:

deepdive.photo_tips: 道路側からは斜面に連なる建物群の全景、近距離では崩落した軒先や増改築の継ぎ目が見どころ。逆光を避け、曇天か柔らかな午前光がまとまりやすい。立入禁止・封鎖区画は撮らない。
deepdive.trivia:

- 2025年には、廃墟を「体験型資源」にする心霊ツアーが実施され、観光活用の先駆例として注目された。
- 湯の山温泉は「鹿の湯」とも呼ばれ、温泉街全体の由来伝承と杉屋の古さが重なっている。
deepdive.warnings_extra: 私有地・立入禁止区画への侵入は厳禁。撮影は道路や公道から行い、地元住民や利用者の迷惑にならないよう静かに見学すること。心霊目的の大声や夜間徘徊は避ける。

deepdive.history_jp_en: Yunoyama Onsen can be documented in historical records from Jokyo 4 (1687), when eight bath houses opened there, and Sugiya Ryokan — said to have been founded in the Genroku era (1688–1704) — is one of the oldest inns representing that early period. According to the [Mie Prefecture Cultural Promotion Foundation](https://www.bunka.pref.mie.lg.jp/rekishi/kenshi/asp/meiji/detail496.html), the origin of the hot spring includes both a tradition that in the Nara period — Yoro 2 (718 CE) — the monk Jōkun discovered it on a revelation from the Yakushi Nyorai (Medicine Buddha), and the legend of the "Deer's Bath (Shika no Yu)" in which a wounded deer healed its wounds in the spring. During the Edo period, bath lodgings were developed under the protection of the Komono Domain, and the name "Yunoyama" became established as a therapeutic spa resort for the Ise and North Ise regions. Following the Satsuma Rebellion of Meiji 10 (1877), a temporary sanatorium for wounded soldiers was established there, and the therapeutic effects were widely promoted, increasing the number of visitors. The founding date of Sugiya Ryokan is most often introduced as the Genroku era (1688–1704), and multiple visitor accounts describe it as "one of the oldest inns in Yunoyama," while some commentary sites also cite Jokyo 4 (1687) as the founding date. [Yunoyama Onsen Arts Festival "Onpaku Yunoyama"](https://www.yunoyama-onsen-art.com/history.html), [YOU Yokkaichi](https://www.you-yokkaichi.com/2025/11/10/41899/), [Haikutu na Hibi](https://haikutu.hatenablog.com/entry/2024/01/17/201228)
deepdive.cultural_context_jp_en: The cluster of ruins at Yunoyama Onsen is a landscape born from the convergence of the post-modern flourishing of hot-spring tourism and the elimination of large-scale inns following the collapse of the bubble economy. The resort town that thrived as a place for therapeutic bathing and leisure became hollowed out by changing demand and aging buildings, and those traces have been made visible as a "ruined hot-spring town." Today, through supernatural tourism, abandoned-site tourism, and event use, questions are being raised about how to share the memory of decline. [Mie Prefecture Cultural Promotion Foundation](https://www.bunka.pref.mie.lg.jp/rekishi/kenshi/asp/meiji/detail496.html), [YOU Yokkaichi](https://www.you-yokkaichi.com/2025/11/10/41899/)
deepdive.local_perspective_jp_en: Locally, for many years the ruins were regarded as a troublesome landscape entailing risks of unauthorized entry and fire, while those associated with the Yunoyama Onsen Association have maintained a watching stance, noting "if tours reduce unauthorized entry, so be it." In the context of regional revitalization, there are moves to treat the ruins not simply as something to be demolished but as resources to be managed and utilized. [YOU Yokkaichi](https://www.you-yokkaichi.com/2025/11/10/41899/), [Tokai TV](https://www.tokai-tv.com/tokainews/feature/article_20220401_17339)
deepdive.related_works_en:
- No notable works on record (no primary sources confirmed for any nationally recognized books, films, or TV programs specifically about Sugiya Ryokan)
- Reference: "Sugiya Ryokan Saikyo Shinrei Tour" (Kyoto Occult Shokai, 2025)
- Reference: Mie Prefecture Cultural Promotion Foundation, "Yunoyama Onsen (Komono Village, Mie County)" (historical commentary, year unconfirmed)

deepdive.best_visit_time_en: Late October to November during the autumn foliage season, late morning to around noon when angled light enters — suitable for exterior photography. A quiet weekday is safest.
deepdive.photo_tips_en: From the road side, the full view of the buildings cascading down the slope is the signature shot; at close range, collapsed eaves and addition-and-alteration joints are points of interest. Avoid backlight; overcast skies or soft morning light are easier to manage overall. Do not photograph off-limits or sealed sections.
deepdive.trivia_en:
- For Sugiya Ryokan, two founding date claims — the Genroku era and Jokyo 4 (1687) — coexist, and the way the antiquity is narrated has itself become a point of interest.
- In 2025, a supernatural tour that turned ruins into an "experiential resource" was held, attracting attention as a pioneering example of tourism utilization.
- Yunoyama Onsen is also called "Shika no Yu (Deer's Bath)," and the founding tradition of the resort town as a whole overlaps with the antiquity of Sugiya.
deepdive.warnings_extra_en: Entering private property or off-limits sections is strictly prohibited. Conduct photography from the road or public areas, and view the site quietly so as not to cause inconvenience to local residents or users. Avoid loud voices and nighttime wandering for supernatural purposes.

name: 化野念仏寺
name_kana: あだしのねんぶつじ
address: 〒616-8436 京都府京都市右京区嵯峨鳥居本化野町17
summary: 嵯峨野の奥深くに位置する浄土宗の寺院。約8,000体もの石仏・石塔が境内にひしめき、古来この地に棄てられた「無縁仏」を空海が供養したのが起源とされる。石仏が積み重なる異様な光景は「日本の心霊スポット」の最高峰に数えられ、8月の灯籠供養（竹灯籠で石仏を照らす）は幻想的すぎて現実感を失う。観光地化されているため安全に体験できるが、その非日常感は本物。
highlights: 8,000体の石仏が境内に密集する「石仏の森」
8月の竹灯籠供養は幻想的すぎて言葉を失う光景
空海ゆかりの「無縁仏供養の地」という霊的な重み
from_kameyama: 車で約1時間50分または近鉄＋JR＋嵐電

deepdive.history_jp: 化野念仏寺（あだしのねんぶつじ）は、寺伝では弘仁年間（810〜824年）に空海（弘法大師）がこの地に五智山如来寺を開き、風葬・埋葬された遺骸を供養したのが起源とされる。のち鎌倉時代初期に法然が念仏道場とし、浄土宗寺院として現在の名になったと伝わる。現本堂は正徳2年（1712年）に寂道上人が再建したもの。境内の「西院の河原」に並ぶ約8,000体の石仏・石塔は、化野一帯に葬られ、長い年月で無縁仏となった墓石を、明治中期に地元協力で集めて供養したものとされる。千灯供養は1905年（明治38年）に地域の地蔵盆と結びついて始まったと京都市資料にある。[京都観光Navi](https://ja.kyoto.travel/tourism/single01.php?category_id=7&tourism_id=224), [京都市資料](https://www.city.kyoto.lg.jp/tokei/cmsfiles/contents/0000165/165271/H2502haifusiryou3-2.pdf)
deepdive.cultural_context_jp: 化野は鳥辺野・蓮台野と並ぶ「葬送の地」とされ、死者を弔う場が、無縁仏供養と景観の記憶装置へと転じた場所である。石仏群は、都市の周縁に置かれた死者を地域社会が回収し、念仏と灯明で慰霊する民俗実践の痕跡でもある。千灯供養は、地蔵盆と結びつくことで、冥福祈願と地域行事を接続し、現代観光の中でも「死者を忘れない」共同体の意味を保っている。[京都市資料](https://www.city.kyoto.lg.jp/tokei/cmsfiles/contents/0000165/165271/H2502haifusiryou3-2.pdf), [京都観光Navi](https://ja.kyoto.travel/tourism/single01.php?category_id=7&tourism_id=224)
deepdive.local_perspective_jp: 京都市資料では、千灯供養は嵯峨鳥居本の町内地蔵盆と連動する行事として説明され、地元の夏行事として定着していることがわかる。現在も町並み保存地区の風情を背景に、地域が観光客を受け入れつつ、供養の場として守り続けている。[京都市資料](https://www.city.kyoto.lg.jp/tokei/cmsfiles/contents/0000165/165271/H2502haifusiryou3-2.pdf)
deepdive.related_works:
- 作品『京都の映画文化と歴史 第12回』（京都市、年不詳）: 化野念仏寺と「西院の河原」、映画人が持ち込んだ地蔵の逸話を紹介。[京都観光Navi](https://ja.kyoto.travel/support/film/culture/volume/12.php)
- 著作『方丈記』（鴨長明、1212年頃）: 化野は無常観を象徴する地として和歌・随筆の文脈で参照される。京都観光Naviが枕詞「化野の露」に言及。[京都観光Navi](https://ja.kyoto.travel/tourism/single01.php?category_id=7&tourism_id=224)
- 番組『千灯供養 無縁仏の冥福祈る…京都・化野念仏寺』（読売テレビ系、2024年）: 祭礼当日の様子を報道。[YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6gJXpS02wDY)

deepdive.best_visit_time: 千灯供養のある8月最終土日の日没前後。静かに見るなら平日の開門直後がよい。
deepdive.photo_tips: 山門〜竹林の参道は午前の斜光で竹が映える。西院の河原は逆光を避け、石仏の奥行きを低い位置から撮ると立体感が出る。供養中は灯明や参拝者の邪魔になる撮影を避ける。
deepdive.trivia:
- 「化野」は「はかない」の意を含み、死と再生の無常観を重ねる地名として語られる。
- 境内の石仏は、もともと散乱・埋没していた墓石を明治中期に集めたものと伝わる。
- 千灯供養は、地蔵盆と結びついた地域行事として明治38年（1905）開始とされる。
deepdive.warnings_extra: 寺院は供養の場なので、大声や立入制限区域での撮影は避ける。千灯供養時は参拝者優先で、フラッシュや長時間の場所取りを控える。石仏・灯明には触れず、静かに歩く。

deepdive.history_jp_en: Adashino Nenbutsu-ji Temple, according to its temple tradition, was founded during the Konin era (810–824 CE) when Kukai (Kobo Daishi) established Gochisan Nyoraiji Temple at this site to provide memorial services for the bodies of the dead who had been left exposed or buried here. It is then said that in the early Kamakura period Honen made it a nembutsu (Pure Land recitation) training hall, and it became a Jodo-shu temple under its current name. The present main hall was rebuilt by the Venerable Jakudo in Shotoku 2 (1712). The approximately 8,000 stone Buddhas and stone pagodas arrayed in the "Saino Kawara" (riverbed of purgatory) section of the precinct are said to have been collected with local cooperation in the mid-Meiji period from among the gravestones that had been buried and scattered across the Adashino area over many years, and memorial services were performed for them. According to Kyoto City materials, the Sento Kuyo (thousand-light memorial service) began in 1905 (Meiji 38) when it became connected with the local Jizo-bon (Jizo festival). [Kyoto Tourism Navi](https://ja.kyoto.travel/tourism/single01.php?category_id=7&tourism_id=224), [Kyoto City document](https://www.city.kyoto.lg.jp/tokei/cmsfiles/contents/0000165/165271/H2502haifusiryou3-2.pdf)
deepdive.cultural_context_jp_en: Adashino is, alongside Toribeno and Rendaino, one of the three traditional "funerary grounds" of Kyoto, and it is a place where a site for mourning the dead was transformed into a memorial installation for unaffiliated spirits and a device for preserving landscape memory. The group of stone Buddhas is also a trace of the folk practice through which local society collected the dead from the city's periphery and consoled them with nembutsu recitation and lamplight. The Sento Kuyo, by connecting with the Jizo-bon, links the prayer for the repose of souls with a local festival, preserving even within contemporary tourism the communal meaning of "not forgetting the dead." [Kyoto City document](https://www.city.kyoto.lg.jp/tokei/cmsfiles/contents/0000165/165271/H2502haifusiryou3-2.pdf), [Kyoto Tourism Navi](https://ja.kyoto.travel/tourism/single01.php?category_id=7&tourism_id=224)
deepdive.local_perspective_jp_en: In Kyoto City materials, the Sento Kuyo is described as an event linked with the Saga-Torii-moto neighborhood's Jizo-bon, indicating that it has taken root as a local summer observance. The site continues to be maintained as a place of memorial service while welcoming tourists, set against the backdrop of the preserved historic townscape. [Kyoto City document](https://www.city.kyoto.lg.jp/tokei/cmsfiles/contents/0000165/165271/H2502haifusiryou3-2.pdf)
deepdive.related_works_en:
- Work: "Kyoto's Film Culture and History, Vol. 12" (Kyoto City, year unconfirmed): Introduces Adashino Nenbutsu-ji, the "Saino Kawara," and the legend of a Jizo statue brought there by filmmakers. [Kyoto Tourism Navi](https://ja.kyoto.travel/support/film/culture/volume/12.php)
- Work: Hojoki (Kamo no Chomei, c. 1212 CE): Adashino is referenced in the context of waka poetry and essays as a place symbolizing the Buddhist concept of impermanence. Kyoto Tourism Navi mentions the poetic epithet "dew of Adashino." [Kyoto Tourism Navi](https://ja.kyoto.travel/tourism/single01.php?category_id=7&tourism_id=224)
- TV program: "Sento Kuyo — Praying for the Souls of the Unaffiliated Dead... Adashino Nenbutsu-ji, Kyoto" (Yomiuri TV network, 2024): News coverage of the festival day. [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6gJXpS02wDY)

deepdive.best_visit_time_en: Around sunset on the final Saturday and Sunday of August, when the Sento Kuyo is held. For a quiet visit, just after the gate opens on a weekday is recommended.
deepdive.photo_tips_en: The approach through the bamboo grove from the temple gate is best photographed with morning angled light to make the bamboo stand out. In the Saino Kawara, avoiding backlight and shooting from a low position toward the depth of the stone Buddha array creates a three-dimensional effect. During the memorial service, avoid photography that obstructs the lamplight or worshippers.
deepdive.trivia_en:
- "Adashino" contains the meaning of "transience" (hakanai) and is often discussed as a place name layering the Buddhist concept of impermanence (mujo) and the cycle of death and rebirth.
- The stone Buddhas in the precinct are said to have been collected in the mid-Meiji period from gravestones that were originally scattered and buried.
- The Sento Kuyo is said to have begun in Meiji 38 (1905) as a local observance connected with the Jizo-bon.
deepdive.warnings_extra_en: As the temple is a place of memorial service, please avoid loud voices and photography in restricted areas. During the Sento Kuyo, worshippers take priority — refrain from flash photography or prolonged occupation of a spot. Do not touch the stone Buddhas or lanterns, and walk quietly.

name: 首塚大明神
name_kana: くびづかだいみょうじん
address: 京都府京都市西京区大枝沓掛町（老ノ坂峠付近）
summary: 源頼光が退治した鬼の頭領・酒呑童子の首が埋められたとされる神社。国道9号線から入る細い山道の突き当たりにあり、周囲は昼でも暗い老ノ坂峠の旧道。本能寺の変で織田信長を討った明智光秀がここで「どうせ後戻りはできぬ」と覚悟を決めたと伝わる場所でもある。観光客がほとんど訪れない「本物の霊場」として地元から恐れられる。
highlights: 「日本三大妖怪の首が埋まっている」という伝説の重み
明智光秀が覚悟を決めた「歴史の変わり目の場所」
廃墟のモーテルが隣接するという現代の怪異との複合
from_kameyama: 車で約1時間30分

deepdive.history_jp: 首塚大明神は、京都市西京区大枝沓掛町の老ノ坂峠付近にある小社で、酒呑童子の首塚と伝えられる。伝承では、源頼光と四天王が大江山で酒呑童子を討った後、その首を都へ運ぶ途中、老ノ坂で急に重くなって動かなくなり、やむなく埋めたという。また、子安地蔵の「都に不浄なものを持ち込むな」との託宣でそこに葬った説や、酒呑童子が死に際に「首から上の病を救う」と誓ったため霊場になった説もある。物語の原型は室町期の『大江山絵詞』にさかのぼるとされ、酒呑童子説話自体は平安後期〜中世に成立・展開したとみられる。現在の社は比較的新しく、昭和60年頃に宗教法人化されたと伝わる。[Wikipedia日本語版](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%A6%96%E5%A1%9A%E5%A4%A7%E6%98%8E%E7%A5%9E), [京都市の石碑案内](https://www2.city.kyoto.lg.jp/somu/rekishi/fm/ishibumi/html/ni015.html), [京都観光Navi](https://ja.kyoto.travel/tourism/single02.php?category_id=7&tourism_id=545)
deepdive.cultural_context_jp: 境界の峠に鬼の首を鎮めるこの地は、都と異界の接点を可視化する霊場として理解できる。疫病除け・怨霊鎮め・首から上の病平癒といった信仰が重なり、恐れと加護が同居する点に民俗宗教の特色がある。観光地化しすぎず、地元が小規模に護持し続けることで、伝承の緊張感が保たれている。[Wikipedia日本語版](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%A6%96%E5%A1%9A%E5%A4%A7%E6%98%8E%E7%A5%9E), [YouTube「京都・丹波の寺社#40」](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LFshTfgxXZ0)
deepdive.local_perspective_jp: 訪問記では、例祭の日に氏子が集まり清掃や祭礼準備をする一方、普段は常駐の神職もなく静かな場所だと記される。地元では「心霊スポット」よりも、首から上の病に霊験がある小さな氏神的存在として受け止められている。[note訪問記](https://note.com/komichi2/n/n1a1dad05b4f1), [note訪問記](https://note.com/komichi2/n/nc99b7e5fc938)

deepdive.best_visit_time: 例祭のある4月上旬〜中旬の午前、または日中の明るい時間帯。
deepdive.photo_tips: 入口の鳥居、細い山道の終点、社殿背後の塚を順に入れる構図が定番。薄暗い林内は午前の斜光が出やすい。柵内・社殿周辺は立入や接写を避け、祭礼中は撮影前に一声かける。
deepdive.trivia:
- 酒呑童子は「首から上の病を救う」と誓ったと伝わり、頭痛・歯痛の参詣先として語られる。
- 老ノ坂は山城と丹波の境界で、都へ不浄を入れない“境目”の民俗感覚が色濃い。
- 近年の訪問記では、雷に打たれた黒焦げの御神木やヒイラギも印象的な見どころとして語られる。
deepdive.warnings_extra: 山中の小社で、参道や柵の内側への無断立入は避ける。祭礼時は地元の準備を優先し、静かに拝観すること。心霊目的の大声や夜間訪問は控え、供物・石などを持ち帰らない。

deepdive.history_jp_en: Kubizuka Daimyojin is a small shrine near Oinosaka Pass in Oshikake-cho, Nishikyo Ward, Kyoto City, and is said to be the burial mound of Shuten Doji's severed head. According to tradition, after Minamoto no Yorimitsu and his Four Heavenly Kings (Shitennō) slew Shuten Doji at Mt. Oe and were carrying the head toward the capital, it suddenly became too heavy to move at Oinosaka, and they had no choice but to bury it there. Alternative accounts also exist: a tradition that the oracle of the Koyasu Jizo ("bring no impurity into the capital") decreed its burial there, and another tradition that because Shuten Doji swore at the moment of death to "heal diseases above the neck" the site became a sacred place. The prototype of this narrative is said to trace back to the Oe-yama Emaki (Illustrated Scroll of Oe-yama) of the Muromachi period, while the Shuten Doji legend itself appears to have been formulated and developed in the late Heian through medieval periods. The present shrine is relatively recent, said to have been formally registered as a religious corporation around 1985 (Showa 60). [Wikipedia (Japanese)](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%A6%96%E5%A1%9A%E5%A4%A7%E6%98%8E%E7%A5%9E), [Kyoto City stone monument guide](https://www2.city.kyoto.lg.jp/somu/rekishi/fm/ishibumi/html/ni015.html), [Kyoto Tourism Navi](https://ja.kyoto.travel/tourism/single02.php?category_id=7&tourism_id=545)
deepdive.cultural_context_jp_en: This site — where the demon's head is pacified at a boundary pass — can be understood as a sacred place that makes visible the junction between the capital and the other world. The overlapping beliefs in epidemic prevention, spirit pacification, and healing of diseases above the neck exhibit the characteristic folk religious quality of fear and protection coexisting. The fact that it has not become overly touristic, and that local people continue to maintain it on a small scale, preserves the tension inherent in the tradition. [Wikipedia (Japanese)](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%A6%96%E5%A1%9A%E5%A4%A7%E6%98%8E%E7%A5%9E), [YouTube "Kyoto and Tanba Shrines and Temples #40"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LFshTfgxXZ0)
deepdive.local_perspective_jp_en: Visitor accounts describe the day of the annual festival (reitaisai) as one when ujiko (parishioners) gather for cleaning and festival preparations, while at other times there are no resident priests and it is a quiet place. Locally it is regarded less as a "supernatural site" and more as a small tutelary deity with efficacy against diseases of the head. [note visit account](https://note.com/komichi2/n/n1a1dad05b4f1), [note visit account](https://note.com/komichi2/n/nc99b7e5fc938)

deepdive.best_visit_time_en: Morning of early to mid-April during the annual festival (reitaisai), or any bright daytime hour.
deepdive.photo_tips_en: A composition sequentially including the torii gate at the entrance, the end of the narrow mountain path, and the mound behind the main hall is standard. Morning angled light is available in the dimly lit forest interior. Avoid entering or taking close-up photographs inside the fence or around the main hall; when a festival is underway, ask permission before photographing.
deepdive.trivia_en:
- Shuten Doji is said to have vowed to "heal diseases above the neck," and the site is described as a place of pilgrimage for headaches and toothaches.
- Oinosaka is on the boundary between Yamashiro and Tamba provinces, and has a strong folkloric sense of being a "boundary" that prevents impurity from entering the capital.
- Recent visitor accounts also describe the scorched and blackened divine tree struck by lightning and a holly tree as impressive highlights.

During festival rites, give priority to local preparations and view quietly. Refrain from loud voices and nighttime visits for supernatural purposes, and do not take away offerings or stones.

name: 鳥辺野（京都の古代葬送地）
name_kana: とりべの
address: 京都府京都市東山区（清水寺〜阿弥陀ヶ峰周辺）
summary: 平安京から江戸時代まで「死体の棄て場」だった地域。東山の清水寺周辺から阿弥陀ヶ峰にかけての一帯は、死者の遺体が風葬・野葬された古代葬送地「鳥辺野」の中心。現在は観光地化されているが、その土の下には無数の骨が眠るとされ、地名・地域伝承に「死」の記憶が刻みこまれている。源氏物語など日本文学にも頻繁に登場する「あの世の入口」として、六道珍皇寺・六道の辻という冥界の入口が現存する。
highlights: 「死体の棄て場」だった場所が現在は日本有数の観光地
「六道の辻」「六道珍皇寺」という冥界の入口が現存
夏の「六道参り」は先祖の霊を呼び戻す伝統行事が現役
from_kameyama: 近鉄＋JRで約1時間30分

deepdive.history_jp: 鳥辺野は、京都東山の阿弥陀ヶ峰山麓に広がった古代以来の葬送地で、平安時代には「風葬・野葬」の場として認識され、近世には火葬地としても扱われたとされる。京都市史は、六波羅が古くは鳥辺野への入口にあたり、六道珍皇寺前が「賽河原」すなわち彼岸と此岸の境界と伝えられたと記す。また、珍皇寺の創建には承和3年（836年）説、空海の師・慶俊による創建説、鳥部氏建立説があり、10世紀末には周辺寺社と境界争論も起きていた。鳥辺野は『源氏物語』や『徒然草』など古典文学にも死と無常の象徴として頻出し、後世の小野篁冥土通い伝説や六道詣りの信仰を支える場所として記憶されてきた。[京都市「都市史09 六波羅」](https://www2.city.kyoto.lg.jp/somu/rekishi/fm/nenpyou/htmlsheet/toshi09.html), [京都観光Navi「六道珍皇寺」](https://ja.kyoto.travel/tourism/single02.php?category_id=7&tourism_id=492), [J-STAGE論文（渡辺・布野, 2001）](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/aija/66/543/66_KJ00004226208/_article/-char/ja/)
deepdive.cultural_context_jp: 鳥辺野は、都の外縁に死者を送り出すための「境界の場所」として生まれ、都市の衛生・宗教・死生観が交差した空間だった。平安京の中心から少し離れた東山の地形が、葬送地の定着を後押ししたと考えられる。現代では観光地の足元に死の記憶を重ねる場所として、無常観や先祖供養を再確認する文化資源になっている。[J-STAGE論文（渡辺・布野, 2001）](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/aija/66/543/66_KJ00004226208/_article/-char/ja/), [京都市「都市史09 六波羅」](https://www2.city.kyoto.lg.jp/somu/rekishi/fm/nenpyou/htmlsheet/toshi09.html)
deepdive.local_perspective_jp: 地元では、六道まいりの時期になると珍皇寺に参拝者が集まり、迎え鐘や高野槙で精霊を迎える行事として受け継がれている。観光地のすぐそばにありながら、氏子・寺院関係者にとっては「死者を迎える」実践の場で、日常の町並みの中に信仰が残っている。[京都観光Navi「精霊迎え 六道まいり」](https://ja.kyoto.travel/event/single.php?event_id=4701), [京都市「都市史09 六波羅」](https://www2.city.kyoto.lg.jp/somu/rekishi/fm/nenpyou/htmlsheet/toshi09.html)

- 作品『徒然草』（吉田兼好、14世紀前半）- 京都の死生観を語る文脈で鳥辺野が想起される。
- 作品『今昔物語集』（12世紀成立）- 六道珍皇寺・小野篁伝説と結びつく京の冥界譚が語られる。
- TV『光る君へ』（NHK、2024年）- 作中で鳥辺野が重要な場面として描かれる。[NHK大河ドラマ「光る君へ」](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%85%89%E3%82%8B%E5%90%9B%E3%81%B8)

deepdive.history_jp_en: Toribeno was an ancient funerary ground spreading across the foothills of Mt. Amida-ga-mine on the eastern hills of Kyoto, recognized in the Heian period as a site of "sky burial and field burial" (fusozo / nosozo) and reportedly used as a cremation site in the early modern period as well. The Kyoto City history notes that Rokuhara was anciently at the entrance to Toribeno, and that the area in front of Rokudo Chinno-ji was called "Sainokawara" — the boundary between this world and the next. The founding of Chinno-ji itself has multiple traditions: Jogan 3 (836 CE), founding by Kyoshu — the teacher of Kukai — or founding by the Toribe clan, and surrounding temples and shrines were involved in boundary disputes in the late 10th century as well. Toribeno appears frequently in classical literature such as The Tale of Genji and Essays in Idleness as a symbol of death and impermanence, and has been remembered as a place supporting the belief in Ono no Takamura's journey to the underworld and the Rokudo-mairi (pilgrimage to the six realms of existence). [Kyoto City "Urban History 09: Rokuhara"](https://www2.city.kyoto.lg.jp/somu/rekishi/fm/nenpyou/htmlsheet/toshi09.html), [Kyoto Tourism Navi "Rokudo Chinno-ji"](https://ja.kyoto.travel/tourism/single02.php?category_id=7&tourism_id=492), [J-STAGE paper (Watanabe & Funo, 2001)](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/aija/66/543/66_KJ00004226208/_article/-char/ja/)
deepdive.cultural_context_jp_en: Toribeno was born as a "boundary place" from which the dead were dispatched beyond the city's perimeter, and was a space where urban hygiene, religion, and attitudes toward death and life intersected. The topography of the Eastern Hills (Higashiyama), slightly removed from the center of the Heian capital, is thought to have facilitated the establishment of the funerary ground there. Today it functions as a cultural resource for reconfirming ideas about impermanence and ancestral memorial services — a place that overlays the memory of death beneath the feet of a tourist destination. [J-STAGE paper (Watanabe & Funo, 2001)](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/aija/66/543/66_KJ00004226208/_article/-char/ja/), [Kyoto City "Urban History 09: Rokuhara"](https://www2.city.kyoto.lg.jp/somu/rekishi/fm/nenpyou/htmlsheet/toshi09.html)
deepdive.local_perspective_jp_en: Locally, during the Rokudo-mairi period, worshippers gather at Chinno-ji and the tradition of welcoming ancestral spirits with the "Mukae-gane" (welcome bell) and koya-maki (Podocarpus macrophyllus) is carried on. Although the site is in the immediate vicinity of a tourist district, for parishioners and temple staff it remains a place for the practice of "welcoming the dead," and faith survives within the everyday townscape. [Kyoto Tourism Navi "Shoryomukae Rokudo-mairi"](https://ja.kyoto.travel/event/single.php?event_id=4701), [Kyoto City "Urban History 09: Rokuhara"](https://www2.city.kyoto.lg.jp/somu/rekishi/fm/nenpyou/htmlsheet/toshi09.html)
deepdive.related_works_en:
- Work: The Tale of Genji (Murasaki Shikibu, early 11th century) — Toribeno is referenced as a symbol of impermanence and death.
- Work: Essays in Idleness (Yoshida Kenko, early 14th century) — Toribeno is evoked in the context of Kyoto's view of death and life.
- Work: Konjaku Monogatarishu (compiled 12th century) — Tales of Kyoto's underworld connected with Rokudo Chinno-ji and the Ono no Takamura legend.
- TV: Hikaru Kimi e (NHK, 2024) — Toribeno is depicted as an important scene in the drama. [Wikipedia "Hikaru Kimi e"](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%85%89%E3%82%8B%E5%90%9B%E3%81%B8)

deepdive.best_visit_time_en: Early morning to evening during the Rokudo-mairi period (August 7–10). For a less crowded visit, a weekday morning is recommended.
deepdive.photo_tips_en: Standard subjects include the stone pillar marking "Rokudo no Tsuji," the entrance to Chinno-ji, and the course of the road extending from Matsubara-dori toward Kiyomizudera. Morning is easier to shoot than the afternoon, which tends toward backlight. As the hall interior and the well have viewing restrictions, confirm photography permissions and avoid unauthorized photography.
deepdive.trivia_en:
- "Rokudo no Tsuji" (Crossroads of the Six Realms) means the junction leading to the six realms of existence; the place name itself preserves an underworld worldview.
- Ono no Takamura is said to have served the imperial court by day and the underworld by night, becoming the legendary centerpiece of Rokudo Chinno-ji.
- Kyoto's three great funerary sites — Toribeno, Adashino, and Rendaino — symbolize the view of death and life at the city's outer margins.
deepdive.warnings_extra_en: In the temple precinct and memorial areas, please avoid loud voices and prolonged occupation of a spot, and give priority to worshippers. The well and hall interior have viewing conditions; confirm permission before photography. Do not obstruct processions or sutra recitation during memorial observances.

name: 犬鳴山トンネル
name_kana: いぬなきやまとんねる
address: 〒598-0023 大阪府泉佐野市（犬鳴山・七宝滝寺方面）
summary: 大阪屈指の心霊トンネルとして有名な犬鳴山トンネル。約1,300年前に役行者が開いた修験道の霊山・犬鳴山の中に位置し、「トンネル内でバックミラーを見てはいけない」という噂が定番。少女・少年の霊が出るとされる。修験道の霊場という背景から霊的な密度が高いとされる。大阪府内で最も「本物の怖さ」に近いと評される場所。七宝滝寺の修行道と心霊スポットが混在する複雑な空間。
highlights: 「バックミラーを見るな」という具体的な注意事項の説得力
修験道の霊山として1,300年の霊的蓄積がある場所
大阪府内で最も「本物の怖さ」に近いと評される場所
from_kameyama: 車で約1時間40分

deepdive.history_jp: 犬鳴山トンネルは、犬鳴山（現・七宝瀧寺を中心とする修験霊場）の山内に通じる道路施設で、山そのものの来歴は寺伝では斉明天皇7年（661年）、役行者が28歳で開いたとされる。七宝瀧寺公式と日本遺産ポータルによれば、山中の瀧で不動明王が現れたことに由来し、山内の七瀑を「七宝充満の智水」とみて寺名が定まったという。さらに天徳年間（957〜961年）には、猟師を救った愛犬の伝説から「犬鳴山」と勅号されたとも伝わる。南北朝・戦国期には中興・再編も重ねられ、現在は修験道の行場と参拝路の中に、後世に心霊スポット化したトンネルが重なっている。([犬鳴山七宝瀧寺 公式](https://inunakisan.jp/about), [日本遺産ポータルサイト](https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/culturalproperties/result/4369/), [泉佐野市観光協会](https://www.kankou-izumisano.jp/50on/a/inunaki.html))
deepdive.cultural_context_jp: 犬鳴山は、滝・山道・修行・温泉が一体化した修験道の場で、山中全体が行場として整えられてきた。人々が「怖さ」を語るのは、単なる怪談というより、霊場に対する畏れと近代以降の都市伝説が結びついた結果とみられる。とくに車道トンネルは、信仰の山に近代交通が入り込んだ境界空間として、神聖さと不安が同居しやすい。([犬鳴山七宝瀧寺 公式](https://inunakisan.jp/about), [泉佐野市観光協会](https://www.kankou-izumisano.jp/50on/a/inunaki.html), [大阪観光局](https://osaka-info.jp/spot/mount-inunaki/))
deepdive.local_perspective_jp: 地元側では、犬鳴山は心霊スポット以前に修行と観光の山として扱われている。七宝瀧寺は護摩祈祷や修行体験を通年で受け入れ、泉佐野市も渓谷・滝・温泉を含む観光資源として案内している。危険な夜間探索より、参拝・登山・温泉利用で訪れてほしいという空気が強い。([犬鳴山七宝瀧寺 公式](https://inunakisan.jp), [泉佐野市観光協会](https://www.kankou-izumisano.jp/50on/a/inunaki.html))

deepdive.trivia:
- 犬鳴山は寺伝で「大峰山より6年早い」開山とされ、修験道の元山上と呼ばれる。
- 山名は、犬が猟師を救った義犬伝説に由来すると伝わる。

deepdive.warnings_extra: 霊場・修行場なので、大声・立入禁止区域への侵入・夜間の騒音は厳禁。参拝路では山道の安全確保を優先し、写真は他の参拝者や修行者の迷惑にならないよう配慮する。

deepdive.history_jp_en: Inunakiyama Tunnel serves as road access to the interior of Inunakiyama (a mountain sacred to Shugendo centered on Shippe Takiji Temple). According to the mountain's own temple tradition, the mountain was opened by En no Gyoja at age 28 in the seventh year of Empress Saimei's reign (661 CE). According to the official Shippe Takiji Temple website and the Japan Heritage portal, the temple's name was established through viewing the seven waterfalls within the mountain as "the water of wisdom filled with seven treasures," originating in the appearance of Fudo Myo-o at a waterfall within the mountain. It is further said that during the Tentoku era (957–961 CE) the mountain received the imperial name "Inunakiyama" (Mountain of the Howling Dog) from a legend of a faithful dog that saved a hunter. The mountain underwent reconstruction and reorganization during the Nanbokucho and Sengoku periods, and today a tunnel — which was later associated with supernatural phenomena — is superimposed on Shugendo sacred grounds and pilgrimage paths. ([Inunakiyama Shippe Takiji Temple official site](https://inunakisan.jp/about), [Japan Heritage portal](https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/culturalproperties/result/4369/), [Izumisano City Tourism Association](https://www.kankou-izumisano.jp/50on/a/inunaki.html))
deepdive.cultural_context_jp_en: Inunakiyama is a Shugendo site where waterfalls, mountain paths, ascetic practice, and hot springs are integrated, and the entire mountain has been developed as a practice ground. People's descriptions of "fear" appear to be less a matter of ghost stories per se and more the result of the reverence for a sacred site intertwining with modern urban legends. The paved road tunnel in particular is a boundary space where modernity's transportation infrastructure has intruded upon a mountain of faith — a space in which the sacred and the anxious easily coexist. ([Inunakiyama Shippe Takiji Temple official site](https://inunakisan.jp/about), [Izumisano City Tourism Association](https://www.kankou-izumisano.jp/50on/a/inunaki.html), [Osaka Tourism Bureau](https://osaka-info.jp/spot/mount-inunaki/))
deepdive.local_perspective_jp_en: On the local side, Inunakiyama is treated before anything as a mountain of ascetic practice and tourism, not as a supernatural site. Shippe Takiji Temple accepts goma (fire ritual) prayers and ascetic practice experiences year-round, and Izumisano City also presents the area as a tourism resource that includes the gorge, waterfalls, and hot springs. There is a strong sense that visitors should come for worship, hiking, and hot-spring bathing rather than dangerous nighttime exploration. ([Inunakiyama Shippe Takiji Temple official site](https://inunakisan.jp), [Izumisano City Tourism Association](https://www.kankou-izumisano.jp/50on/a/inunaki.html))

- Book/subject: "The Inunaki-mura Legend" in various ghost story / urban legend collections (multiple authors, reprinted from around 2009)
- TV/video: Omagadoki Film (supernatural verification channel, from 2022) — includes an Inunakiyama Tunnel episode

deepdive.best_visit_time_en: A weekday morning in the fresh greenery season, May to June, or the bright daytime hours in early November during the autumn foliage.
deepdive.photo_tips_en: The gorge around the Inunakiyama bus stop, the stone steps leading to Shippe Takiji Temple, and combinations of waterfalls and mountain paths are the main subjects. Around the tunnel it is dark with poor footing, so photograph the entrance exterior wide-angle during daytime. Avoid photographing or entering off-limits or sealed sections.
deepdive.trivia_en:
- According to temple tradition, Inunakiyama was opened "six years earlier than Mt. Omine" and is called the "original Oku-no-in" of Shugendo.
- The mountain's name is said to derive from a legend of a loyal dog that saved a hunter.
- Also known as the "Women's Omine" (Nyonin Omine), the feature that female practitioners can train there is a distinguishing characteristic.
deepdive.warnings_extra_en: As a sacred site and training ground, loud voices, entry into off-limits areas, and nighttime noise are strictly prohibited. On the pilgrimage path, prioritize safety on the mountain trail and be considerate so that photography does not inconvenience other worshippers and practitioners.

name: 鵺塚
name_kana: ぬえづか
address: 大阪府大阪市北区中之島付近（他にも複数箇所）
summary: 源頼政が退治した怪物「鵺（ぬえ）」の死骸が流れ着いたとされる塚が大阪の各地に点在する。鵺は「頭が猿、胴が狸、尾が蛇、足が虎」という合成怪物で、「正体不明なもの」の代名詞として現代語にも残る。都市開発で場所が不明確になりながらも「鵺の呪い」として伝承が続く。大阪の繁華街の足元に沈んだ「怪物の骨」という都市伝説の重みが一生忘れられない体験を提供する。
highlights: 日本最有名な怪物「鵺」の埋葬地が大阪市内に点在
「鵺＝正体不明」という概念が生まれた聖地
繁華街の真下に眠る「呪いの骨」というコントラスト
from_kameyama: 近鉄＋地下鉄で約1時間30分

deepdive.history_jp: 鵺塚は、大阪市都島区都島本通3丁目18、母恩寺東北の旧沢上江村の野中にあるとされる塚で、『平家物語』に見える鵺の遺骸を葬った伝承地です。大阪市の史跡解説によれば、近衛天皇を悩ませた怪鳥を源頼政が射落とし、死骸を船に乗せて淀川へ流したところ、澤上江の渚に漂着し、祟りを恐れた村人が母恩寺の住職に告げて土に埋め、塚を築いたと伝わります。江戸初期の地誌『芦分船』にはすでに紹介があり、少なくとも17世紀前半には地域伝承として定着していたことがうかがえます。なお、鵺の漂着地は大阪市内のほか芦屋にも伝わり、『摂津名所図会』は両説について「いづれも論ずるにたらん」としています。現在の塚は明治3年（1870）に大阪府が改修し、祠は昭和32年（1957）に地元の人々が改修したものです。([大阪市 都島区の史跡](https://www.city.osaka.lg.jp/miyakojima/page/0000016853.html), [大阪市 ぬえ塚](https://www.city.osaka.lg.jp/kensetsu/page/0000010002.html), [Wikipedia「鵺」](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%B5%BA))
deepdive.cultural_context_jp: 鵺塚は、正体不明の災厄を「怪物の遺骸」として可視化し、土地に鎮める御霊・鎮魂の発想を示す伝承地です。都市の縁辺で生まれたこの物語は、淀川水運と大阪湾の流れを背景に、怪異を地理へ接続して記憶する民俗的な仕組みでもあります。現代では、繁華街の近くに残る小さな塚として、都市化の中で失われがちな土地の記憶を支える文化資源になっています。([大阪市 都島区の史跡](https://www.city.osaka.lg.jp/miyakojima/page/0000016853.html), [Wikipedia「鵺」](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%B5%BA))
deepdive.local_perspective_jp: 大阪市の案内では、鵺塚は「300年以上も前から鵺の墓として、地元の人々によって祀られてきた」とされ、現在も毎年8月24日に祭りがあると紹介されています。地元では、失われかけた伝承を守る小さな信仰対象として扱われているようです。([大阪市 いちょう並木PDF](https://www.manabi.city.osaka.lg.jp/contents/lll/ityou03/ityou/buckup/201308_p22.pdf), [大阪市 都島区の史跡](https://www.city.osaka.lg.jp/miyakojima/page/0000016853.html))
deepdive.related_works:
- 『平家物語』（作者未詳、13世紀成立）: 源頼政の鵺退治と、その死骸を流した後日譚の典拠。
- 『摂津名所図会』（秋里籬嶌、1796-1798）: 摂津の名所として鵺塚伝承を記す地誌。
- 『芦分船』（江戸初期）: 鵺の死骸が大阪側へ流れ着いたとする古い地誌的記述。
- テレビ・映像作品: 特記事項なし（本件調査では鵺塚そのものを主題にした公的な代表作は確認できず）。

- 現在の塚は、明治期の改修と昭和期の祠修復で今に伝えられています。([大阪市 ぬえ塚](https://www.city.osaka.lg.jp/kensetsu/page/0000010002.html))
deepdive.warnings_extra: 住宅地の中の小さな史跡なので、長居や大声は避け、参拝・撮影は短時間で静かに行うのが無難です。私有地に見える場所では無断立ち入りをしないよう注意してください。

deepdive.history_jp_en: Nuetsuka is said to be a burial mound formerly located in the open field of the old Sawakamie Village in 3-chome 18, Miyakojima-Hondori, Miyakojima Ward, Osaka City, near the northeast of Boon-ji Temple, and is identified as the traditional site where the body of the nue (a mythical creature) described in The Tale of the Heike was buried. According to Osaka City's historical site explanation, after Minamoto no Yorimasa shot down the monstrous bird that had been plaguing Emperor Konoe, the carcass was placed on a boat and floated down the Yodo River, washed ashore at the beach of Sawakamie, and the villagers — fearing a curse — informed the head priest of Boon-ji Temple and buried it, piling up a mound. The site is already introduced in the early Edo period gazetteer Ashiwake-bune, suggesting that it had taken root as a local tradition by at least the first half of the 17th century. It should be noted that the landing place of the nue is also said in another tradition to be Ashiya, and the early Edo era Settsu Meisho Zue takes the position "either tradition is worth discussing." The present mound was renovated by Osaka Prefecture in Meiji 3 (1870), and the shrine was renovated by local residents in 1957 (Showa 32). ([Osaka City — Miyakojima Ward Historical Sites](https://www.city.osaka.lg.jp/miyakojima/page/0000016853.html), [Osaka City — Nuetsuka](https://www.city.osaka.lg.jp/kensetsu/page/0000010002.html), [Wikipedia "Nue"](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%B5%BA))
deepdive.cultural_context_jp_en: Nuetsuka is a traditional site that demonstrates the idea of making visible an unidentified calamity as "a monster's corpse" and pacifying it in the land — a concept of pacification of vengeful spirits and requiem for the dead. This narrative, born at the urban periphery, is also a folkloric mechanism for connecting the uncanny to geography and preserving it in memory, set against the background of Yodo River water transportation and Osaka Bay currents. Today, as a small mound surviving near a busy district, it functions as a cultural resource supporting land memory that tends to be lost in the process of urbanization. ([Osaka City — Miyakojima Ward Historical Sites](https://www.city.osaka.lg.jp/miyakojima/page/0000016853.html), [Wikipedia "Nue"](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%B5%BA))
deepdive.local_perspective_jp_en: In Osaka City's description, Nuetsuka is said to have been "venerated by local people as the grave of the nue for more than 300 years," and an annual festival is noted for August 24. Locally it appears to be treated as a small object of faith preserving a nearly lost tradition. ([Osaka City — Ginkgo Tree PDF](https://www.manabi.city.osaka.lg.jp/contents/lll/ityou03/ityou/buckup/201308_p22.pdf), [Osaka City — Miyakojima Ward Historical Sites](https://www.city.osaka.lg.jp/miyakojima/page/0000016853.html))
deepdive.related_works_en:
- The Tale of the Heike (anonymous, compiled 13th century): Primary source for the Minamoto no Yorimasa nue-slaying episode and the subsequent account of disposing of the carcass.
- Settsu Meisho Zue (Akisato Rito, 1796–1798): A gazetteer of famous places in Settsu that records the Nuetsuka tradition.
- Ashiwake-bune (early Edo period): An early gazetteer-style description stating that the nue's carcass drifted to the Osaka side.
- TV/audiovisual works: No notable works on record (no publicly representative primary works specifically about Nuetsuka confirmed in this research).
